# Extensions

The `extensions` input loads two kinds of packages into pi-action:

- **pi extensions** give model **providers**. pi-action uses only the providers that they register. See [Providers](#providers).
- **pi-durable extensions** give **tools and prompt sections** to every conversation. Their tools can ask questions, which pi-action posts on the issue or pull request. See [pi-durable extensions](#pi-durable-extensions).

An extension is code that runs inside pi-action, with all the permissions of the job. Load only extensions that you trust. See [Security](security.md#extensions).

## Declare extensions

Write one extension per line, or separate them with commas. pi-action ignores empty lines and `#` comments. A comment can be a full line, or it can follow a spec after a space. The `#` in a git ref such as `github:owner/repo#v1.0.0` is not a comment, because no space comes before it:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    extensions: |
      # pi-durable extensions
      github:cv/pit#v0.35.0          # pit's typescript tool
      # pi extensions (providers)
      @acme/pi-provider@1.4.2        # from npm, pinned
      ./.pi/extensions/gateway.ts    # in this repository
```

### Sources

- **npm package spec**: `name`, `name@1.2.3`, `@scope/name@^1`, `npm:name`, or `github:owner/repo#ref`.
- **Path**: a value that starts with `./`, `../`, `/`, or `~/`. pi-action resolves it against the workspace (or the home directory, for `~/`).
- pi-action does not support the `git:` sources of pi. Use the npm form `github:owner/repo#ref`.

### Installation

- pi-action installs npm packages into a new directory in `RUNNER_TEMP`, never into your repository. It runs `npm install --ignore-scripts --legacy-peer-deps --omit=dev`.
- npm does not get the `INPUT_*` variables of the action (`github_token`, `api_key`).
- Lifecycle scripts do not run. Thus, packages that need a build step or native modules do not work.
- pi-action does not install the pi packages of an extension (its `peerDependencies`). Imports of `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, `@earendil-works/pi-durable`, and `@earendil-works/chord` (and their subpaths) get the copies of pi-action. Thus, the extension and pi-action share one instance of each.
- pi-action loads paths where they are. It does not install them.
- pi-action runs TypeScript without a build step, with [jiti](https://github.com/unjs/jiti), as pi does.
- If an extension does not load, the run fails.

## Providers

pi-action finds the entry points of a pi extension as pi does:

1. The `pi.extensions` list in `package.json`.
2. If there is no list: the files in the `extensions/` directory (one level deep).
3. If there is no directory: `index.ts` or `index.js`.

From a pi extension, pi-action uses only `pi.registerProvider()`. Both forms work:

- A complete pi-ai `Provider`.
- A name and a config: `baseUrl`, `api`, `apiKey`, `headers`, `authHeader`, `models`, `streamSimple`, and `refreshModels`. If you register a built-in name with only `baseUrl` or `headers`, the built-in provider uses your gateway and keeps its models.

The `apiKey` of a provider config works as in pi: `$ENV_VAR`, `${ENV_VAR}`, `!command`, or a literal key. The `api_key` input has priority when it is set.

pi-action ignores these parts of a pi extension and writes a warning to the log:

- Tools, commands, event handlers, UI, flags, and all other features of the pi coding agent. The agent keeps the read, write, edit, and bash tools of pi-action.
- `oauth` logins, because they cannot run on a runner. Use an API key.
- Image models and classifier models.

To select a provider from an extension, see [Models](models.md#providers-from-pi-extensions).

## pi-durable extensions

A [pi-durable](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-durable) extension adds its tools and prompt sections to every conversation: comment mode, `pr_number` runs, and direct prompts. An example is the `pit/durable` extension of [pit](https://github.com/cv/pit):

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    extensions: |
      github:cv/pit#v0.35.0   # pit's typescript tool (pit/durable)
```

### Package format

- A package is a pi-durable extension package when its `package.json` has `pi.durable`, a module path. Example: `"pi": { "durable": "./src/durable/index.ts" }`.
- The module exports `createPiDurableExtension(options)`, or a default export with the same signature.
- The function returns a pi-durable `Extension`: `{ name, tools?, sections?, hooks?, wraps?, tasks? }`.
- If a package has `pi.durable` and `pi.extensions`, pi-action loads only the `pi.durable` entry, because its pi extensions need the pi coding agent. pi-action writes this to the log.
- pi-action installs the extensions after its coding tools (read, write, edit, bash). Each extension must have a unique name.

### Host options

`createPiDurableExtension` receives `{ cwd, agentDir, trustProject, ui, log }`:

| Option | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `cwd` | The workspace |
| `agentDir` | `agent_dir`, resolved against the workspace. If `agent_dir` is empty: a new temporary directory in `RUNNER_TEMP` |
| `trustProject` | The `trust_project` input |
| `ui` | `{ ask, notify }`, the GitHub UI (see [Questions on GitHub](#questions-on-github)). Only in `comment` mode on an issue or pull request. Not set in `output` mode or for direct prompts |
| `log` | The log of the action (`info`, `warning`) |

pi-durable extensions run in the process of pi-action. Thus, pi-action also sets `GH_TOKEN` and the git identity in its own environment when it loads such an extension. See [Security](security.md#the-agents-github-token-and-git-identity).

### `trust_project`

`trust_project` (default `false`) tells the extension that it can load and run the configuration of the repository. For pit, this is `.pi/pit.json` and `.pi/functions`.

Anyone who can push a branch or open a pull request can change those files. Set `trust_project: true` only for repositories whose code you already run. Do not set it in workflows that run on pull requests from people you do not trust.

## Questions on GitHub

A tool can ask its user a question with `ui.confirm`, `ui.select`, or `ui.input`. (pit asks with its `ui.*` globals, and also when it promotes a function to the project.) pi-action posts the question as a comment on the issue or pull request, and **the run ends**. An answer starts a new run, which continues the thread.

pi-action does not wait for the answer, because people can take hours or days to answer.

### The sequence

1. The tool calls `ui.ask` of pi-action. pi-action posts the question and returns its URL immediately. pit stops the program (the calls that it made before the question keep their effects) and ends the turn with "Question posted: ...".
2. The run ends quietly. pi-action posts no `pi Response` comment. The log tells which question pi waits for. pi-action saves the thread as usual.
3. A person answers: they tick a box (an `issue_comment` `edited` event), or they reply `/answer ...` (an `issue_comment` `created` event). The answer starts a new run on the same thread.
4. pi-action checks who answered (see [Security](security.md#answers-to-questions)). It edits the question to show `✅ Answered: <answer> by @user`. It adds the answer to the conversation as a message to pi, together with a `ui.answer` entry. The message is `**@user** answered pi's question *<title>* (<url>): <answer>`.
5. pi runs its step again. When the program asks the same question, pit returns the answer and does not ask again. Each answer is used one time. If the program asks the same question later, pi-action asks again.

The workflow must listen to `issue_comment` `edited` events. Its `if:` filter must let these events and `/answer` replies through. Use the workflow of the [quick start](../README.md#quick-start). pi-action ignores edits of other comments.

### Kinds of questions

| Kind | The comment | How to answer | The value pit gets |
|------|-------------|---------------|--------------------|
| `confirm` | Two boxes: `- [ ] Yes` and `- [ ] No` | Tick one box | `true` for Yes, `false` for No |
| `select` | One box for each option (each option on one line) | Tick one box | The text of the option |
| `input` | A request for a reply | Write a comment that starts with `/answer`, for example `/answer release-2.1` | The text after `/answer` |

- For `confirm` and `select`, the first box that you tick is the answer. pi-action ignores ticks on a question that has an answer.
- An `/answer` reply goes to the `input` question that it quotes (GitHub's *Quote reply*). Without a quote, it goes to the oldest open `input` question. pi-action adds 👍 to the reply.
- pi-action never takes a question or an `/answer` reply as an `@pi` request, also when it contains `@pi`.

### Special cases

- **The same question two times.** While a question is open, pi-action does not post it again. pi waits for the open question.
- **A run that GitHub cancelled.** GitHub keeps only one pending run for each concurrency group. When more events for the issue come while a run works, GitHub can cancel the run for your answer. To answer again, untick and tick the box, or reply `/answer` again.
- **Notifications.** `ui.notify` writes to the log and to the job summary, not to comments.
# Prompts and templates

pi receives three kinds of messages. `prompt_template` changes only the first kind:

| Message | When | Content |
|---------|------|---------|
| **First message** | The first request of a new thread. A direct prompt always has a new thread | The built-in prompt, or your `prompt_template` |
| **Follow-up** | Each later request on the thread: an `@pi` comment, or a `pr_number` run | `**@login** commented (<url>):` and the task. For a review comment: `commented on the diff`. pi-action adds the URL when it has one. Then the [reply reminder](#the-reply) |
| **Answer** | An answer to a question from a pi-durable extension | `**@login** answered pi's question *<title>* (<url>): <answer>` (see [Extensions](extensions.md#questions-on-github)). Then the [reply reminder](#the-reply) |

A follow-up does not repeat the issue or the diff, because the thread already has them. Thus, when a pull request gets new commits, pi does not get a new diff automatically. Ask pi to look at the changes (for example, `@pi review the new commits`): its tools can run `git` and `gh`. See [Durable threads](threads.md).

## The task

The **task** is the text after the first occurrence of the trigger phrase, without spaces at the start and end. The match ignores case. For `@pi please review this`, the task is `please review this`.

Before pi-action finds the task, it removes HTML comments and invisible characters from the text. It does the same to the title and the body of the issue or pull request (see [Security](security.md#what-pi-action-removes-from-text)).

For a `pr_number` run, the task is `prompt`, or `Please review this pull request` when `prompt` is empty. For a direct prompt, the task is `prompt`.

## The built-in prompt

For an issue or a pull request, the built-in first message has these parts, in this sequence:

1. `# GitHub Issue #<number>` or `# GitHub Pull Request #<number>`.
2. `## Title` and `## Description`: the title and body of the issue or pull request.
3. Pull requests only: `## Existing PR Review Comments`, when the pull request has review comments.
4. `## Task`: the task.
5. `output_mode: comment` only: `## Your Reply`, which tells pi not to post its reply itself (see [The reply](#the-reply)).
6. `## Important: Artifact and Script Requirements`: an instruction to commit and push all work, because the runner and its files are deleted after the run.
7. Pull requests only: `## PR Diff`, the diff of the pull request.

For a direct prompt, the message has `# Direct pi Task`, the task, and the requirements block.

## The reply

In `output_mode: comment`, pi-action posts pi's final response as a comment. pi's tools have the token as `GH_TOKEN`, so pi can also post comments with `gh`. If pi posted its reply itself, the issue would get the same answer twice. Thus, pi-action tells pi not to do this:

- The built-in first message has a `## Your Reply` section.
- Each follow-up and each answer ends with this reminder: _(pi-action posts your final response as a comment here. Don't also post it with `gh`.)_ Threads that began before this reminder existed get it too.

In `output_mode: output`, the reply goes to the `response` output, and the messages do not have this text. A [custom template](#custom-templates) replaces the `## Your Reply` section too, but follow-ups and answers still get the reminder.

## Custom templates

`prompt_template` replaces the **complete** built-in first message. pi-action does not add the requirements block to your template. If you want pi to commit and push its work, write this in your template.

pi-action uses the built-in prompt when `prompt_template` is empty or has only spaces.

### Variables

| Variable | Value | Example |
|----------|-------|---------|
| `{{type}}` | `issue`, `pull_request`, or `direct` | `issue` |
| `{{type_display}}` | `Issue`, `Pull Request`, or `Direct Task` | `Pull Request` |
| `{{number}}` | Number of the issue or pull request. `0` for a direct prompt | `42` |
| `{{title}}` | Title of the issue or pull request, without HTML comments and invisible characters. `Direct prompt` for a direct prompt | `Fix login bug` |
| `{{body}}` | Body of the issue or pull request, without HTML comments and invisible characters. Empty for a direct prompt | The full description |
| `{{task}}` | The [task](#the-task) | `please review this code` |
| `{{diff}}` | Diff of the pull request. Empty for issues and direct prompts | A unified diff |
| `{{reviewComments}}` | The `## Existing PR Review Comments` section. Empty when there are none, and for issues | A Markdown section |
| `{{trigger_comment}}` | The full text that contains the trigger phrase, after pi-action removes HTML comments and invisible characters. The task, for `pr_number` runs and direct prompts | `@pi please review this code` |

### Rules

- pi-action replaces `{{name}}` with the value of the variable. Names are case-sensitive.
- pi-action does not change unknown variables. For example, `{{author}}` stays `{{author}}`.
- pi-action inserts values as they are, in one pass. If an issue body contains `{{diff}}`, the text `{{diff}}` stays in the message.
- There are no conditions or loops (for example `{{#if}}`). An empty variable gives empty text. Thus, `{{diff}}` in a template for issues is harmless. To use different templates for issues and pull requests, use different workflows.

pi-action applies it to:

- The text that contains the trigger phrase: the comment, or the body of an issue or pull request that started pi. This gives the task and `{{trigger_comment}}`.
- The title and the body of the issue or pull request (in the built-in prompt, and in `{{title}}` and `{{body}}`), also for `pr_number` runs.
- `/answer` replies, and the titles of questions.

pi-action does **not** apply it to the diff or to review comments. The model gets this text as it is on GitHub. Also, removing hidden text does not stop prompt injection in visible text.

## Extensions

An extension that you load with `extensions` runs inside pi-action, with the permissions and the environment of the job. It can read `github_token`, `api_key`, and all secrets in the `env` of the step. It can change your repository.

- Load only extensions that you trust.
- Pin npm versions (`name@1.2.3`) or git refs (`github:owner/repo#v1.2.3`).
- Prefer a copy that you reviewed and committed to the repository (a path).
- Keep `trust_project` off, unless you trust all people who can change the repository. See [Extensions](extensions.md#trust_project).

## Thread contents are visible

pi-action stores the full conversation in `refs/pi/threads/<number>`, also the output of tools. It stores the files that pi leaves uncommitted in `refs/pi/worktrees/<number>`, also untracked files that git does not ignore. All people who can read the repository can read these refs. The workflow log shows the arguments of each tool call and the last 30 lines of its output (see [The workflow log](how-it-works.md#the-workflow-log)); GitHub masks registered secrets in the log, but not in the refs. pi-action stops the runner from running workflow commands (such as `::error::` or `::add-mask::`) in the text of pi and in the output of tools. Keep secrets away from the agent, as for all CI jobs. Make git ignore files with secrets, or list them in `worktree_snapshot_exclude`. See [Durable threads](threads.md#read-a-thread) and [Working-tree continuity](threads.md#working-tree-continuity).
## Inputs

Only `github_token` is necessary. All other inputs have a default or are optional. [`action.yml`](action.yml) defines the inputs, and [`src/defaults.ts`](src/defaults.ts) holds the defaults. Tests ([`src/action-docs.test.ts`](src/action-docs.test.ts) and [`src/defaults.test.ts`](src/defaults.test.ts)) make sure that the table below agrees with both files.

| Input | Description | Required | Default |
|-------|-------------|----------|---------|
| `github_token` | GitHub token for the API (issues, pull requests, reactions, comments). The agent's tools also get it as `GH_TOKEN` (see [Security](docs/security.md#the-agents-github-token-and-git-identity)) | Yes | - |
| `api_key` | API key for the selected `provider`, for this run only. Provider environment variables are the preferred alternative (see [Models](docs/models.md#authentication)) | No | - |
| `trigger_phrase` | Text that starts pi. The match ignores case | No | `@pi` |
| `allowed_bots` | Comma-separated bot logins that can start pi | No | - |
| `allowed_users` | Comma-separated GitHub logins that can start pi. When set, only these users can start pi, and `allowed_associations` has no effect | No | - |
| `allowed_associations` | Comma-separated author associations that can start pi when `allowed_users` is empty | No | `OWNER,MEMBER` |
| `timeout` | Seconds before pi-action stops the run. pi-action saves the thread before it stops | No | `1800` |
| `poll_interval` | Seconds between checks for new comments while pi works | No | `15` |
| `provider` | LLM provider (`anthropic`, `openai`, `google`, a custom name, or a provider from an extension) | No | `anthropic` |
| `model` | Model ID | No | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| `provider_base_url` | Base URL of one custom provider and model. Set it to enable the `provider_*` and `model_*` inputs below (see [Models](docs/models.md#a-custom-provider-and-model)) | No | - |
| `provider_api` | API type of the custom provider | No | `openai-completions` |
| `provider_api_key` | Key of the custom provider: a literal key, or the name of an environment variable | No | - |
| `provider_auth_header` | Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` to the custom provider | No | `false` |
| `model_name` | Display name of the custom model | No | - |
| `model_reasoning` | The custom model supports reasoning (thinking) | No | `false` |
| `model_input` | Comma-separated input types of the custom model (`text` or `text,image`) | No | `text` |
| `model_context_window` | Context window of the custom model, in tokens | No | `128000` |
| `model_max_tokens` | Maximum output tokens of the custom model (reasoning counts toward it). A response that hits it with no tool call is continued, up to 3 times in a row and within `timeout`; partial text is posted, marked as cut off. If it keeps hitting the limit, pi posts an error that says so: raise this value, up to the provider's limit for the model | No | `16384` |
| `compat_supports_developer_role` | The OpenAI-compatible custom provider supports developer role messages | No | - |
| `compat_supports_reasoning_effort` | The OpenAI-compatible custom provider supports `reasoning_effort` | No | - |
| `compat_force_adaptive_thinking` | Use adaptive thinking for an Anthropic-compatible custom model (`provider_api: anthropic-messages`). Claude Opus 4.6+ and Sonnet 4.6+ need it | No | - |
| `extensions` | pi extensions and pi-durable extensions to load: npm package specs or workspace paths, one per line or comma-separated (see [Extensions](docs/extensions.md)) | No | - |
| `trust_project` | Let pi-durable extensions load and run the configuration of the repository (see [Extensions](docs/extensions.md#trust_project)) | No | `false` |
| `agent_dir` | Agent directory (user-level state) for pi-durable extensions, relative to the workspace | No | (a new temporary directory in `RUNNER_TEMP`) |
| `worktree_snapshots` | Save the files pi leaves uncommitted with the thread, and restore them at the start of the next run (see [Working-tree continuity](docs/threads.md#working-tree-continuity)) | No | `true` |
| `worktree_snapshot_exclude` | Globs (as in `.gitignore`) of untracked files never to save in a snapshot, one per line or comma-separated, for example `.env*, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa*`. Ignored files are never saved | No | - |
| `prompt_template` | Template for the first message of a new thread (see [Prompts](docs/prompts.md#custom-templates)) | No | (built-in prompt) |
| `output_mode` | `comment`: post to the issue or pull request. `output`: set the step outputs only | No | `comment` |
| `prompt` | Task for the agent. Without `pr_number`, it needs `output_mode: output` (see [Workflow recipes](docs/workflows.md#output-mode-and-direct-prompts)) | No | - |
| `pr_number` | Pull request to work on, for events without one (for example `workflow_dispatch`) | No | - |

### How pi-action reads input values

- Lists (`allowed_*`) are comma-separated. pi-action removes spaces around each item. Logins ignore case and a leading `@`. Associations ignore case.
- `extensions` accepts commas and new lines. pi-action ignores empty lines and `#` comments: a full line, or the rest of a line after a spec and a space.
- Boolean inputs accept `true`, `1`, `yes`, `y`, `on` and `false`, `0`, `no`, `n`, `off`, in any case.
- When a number or boolean input has a value that is not valid, pi-action uses the default.
- Any `output_mode` value other than `output` means `comment`.

## Outputs
